findings.claim_defeated: That no count is offered here.
findings.observed: A count is offered in the same clause: 'five different wordings'. On the natural parse, 'them' binds to the nearest plural noun phrase, 'five different wordings', and the sentence then says it offers no count of the things it has just counted. A strained parse rescues it - 'them' binding to container claims as propositions, so the sentence counts wordings while declining to count claims - and that is evidently what was meant, since the withdrawn text counted claims ordinally ('the fourth container claim ... and the fourth to be withdrawn'). But the distinction between a wording and a claim is exactly what makes the count contestable in the first place, so leaning on it to say no count is offered is circular. The commit message repeats the same construction: 'five distinct wordings have stood, two are withdrawn by name, and one was removed without any withdrawal at all. No count is offered now.' Three counts, then a denial that any is offered.
findings.why_it_matters: The sentence's job is to be the careful replacement for a count that went wrong. A replacement that contradicts itself in one clause invites a reader to distrust the withdrawal it carries. It is also the fourth commit in a row in which this passage's arithmetic has been a finding: 291ec48 wrote a false container claim, 3a8c199 wrote an unre-derived ordinal, and 6170031 writes a count alongside a denial that it counts.
findings.why_it_does_not_block: Nothing measured depends on it. 'Five' is derivable and I derived it independently and got five; the withdrawal it accompanies is sound; and the sentence's load-bearing content is true. It is a wording defect in prose, repairable by deleting five words.

findings.repair_shape_if_wanted: Not mine to build. Either drop 'and no count of them is offered here', or drop 'five different wordings' and keep the denial. Keeping both is what makes it contestable.
